subject: Onramp plan and acceptance gates for Private VPC — commercial sequencing
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onramp plan and acceptance gates for Private VPC — commercial sequencing

Hi Ellen / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the fit for your private VPC deployment. I wanted to propose a concrete onramp plan that ties the evaluation checkpoints to commercial steps so we can align procurement, security review, and engineering enablement. The goal is to close a binding commercial arrangement by the end of September while letting your SREs and security team complete their functional tests in parallel.

High-level ask: can procurement review the attached one-page onramp draft and confirm the acceptable acceptance gates below? If so, we will produce a detailed commercial sequence (pricing spreadsheet + DocuSign bundle) that maps discounts and platform fee ramps to the acceptance gates.

Proposed acceptance gates (evaluation -> production):
- Gate A (Pilot deploy): Private VPC provisioned, basic throughput validated (internal smoke tests) — 2 week window
- Gate B (Performance verification): 99th pct latency targets met under simulated load for 48 hours; KV cache behavior validated
- Gate C (Security signoff): SOC2 evidence provided, network config and KMS integration validated
- Gate D (Commit): Annual capacity commit signed; platform fee scheduling agreed

Commercial sequencing notes (summary):
- We can provide evaluation credits to cover Gate A/B lab usage.
- Discounts on unit price phase in at Gate D based on committed nodes/month.
- Platform fee is typically billed annually; we can amortize for accounting if required.

Attached: onramp-draft.pdf with a suggested timeline and responsibilities.

If this approach looks reasonable I'll loop in our commercial lead to propose precise $ and ramp buckets. Looking to align calendars — what procurement review cadence works for you?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0118

Attachment: onramp-draft.pdf (1 page, PDF)
From: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@acme.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp plan and acceptance gates for Private VPC — commercial sequencing

Thanks Jasmine — the proposed gates are helpful. Quick clarifying questions before procurement schedules a formal review:

1) For Gate B (performance verification) can you define the load profile you intend to run and an expected token/sec baseline? Our SREs need that to ensure the simulated traffic is realistic.
2) For the platform fee, procurement prefers an annual flat fee. Will you provide an option to amortize for ARR accounting?
3) Please send a pricing workbook tied to ramp steps (we will need line items the CFO can present).

We will kick off Security review next week and will attach the results to your Gate C. Also please include the SOC2 report stub and any runbooks for key rotation.

Thanks — Ellen
Ellen Shaw
Head of Procurement, Acme AI
procurement@acme.ai

Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp plan and acceptance gates for Private VPC — commercial sequencing

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear questions. I’m attaching a pricing workbook that maps 3 ramp buckets to discounts and platform fee options; summary below.

Attachment: commercial-sequence-v1.xlsx (pricing & ramp model)

Executive summary (short):
- Ramp buckets: Pilot (0-10 nodes), Scale-1 (11-50 nodes), Scale-2 (51+ nodes).
- Unit pricing: tiered per-token effective rates that reduce at Scale-1 and Scale-2 commit thresholds.
- Platform fee options: (A) Standard annual $Xk fee; (B) Lower annual fee + higher unit rate; (C) No platform fee for first year with a modest uplift on unit pricing.
- Evaluation credits: we’ll allocate $25k in credits for Gate A/B testing that won’t be billed unless you progress to Gate D.
- DocuSign: we can prepare a term sheet and a staged SOW keyed to the Gate D commit (link below).

Proposed timeline to close:
- Week of Aug 9: Procurement & Security review
- Week of Aug 23: Final commercial proposal and legal redlines
- Week of Sep 6: Execute term sheet and finalize onboarding dates

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/xyz123-sign
HubSpot deal: https://app.redwood.com/hubspot/deal/ACME-2027-08

If you prefer, we can present the workbook to your finance team on a short call. Marissa, would you be available to join for a technical runbook overview?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

> On Aug 2, 2027, at 10:25 AM, Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@acme.ai> wrote:

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.ai>, Legal <legal@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp plan and acceptance gates for Private VPC — commercial sequencing

Thanks for the workbook — high level feedback from Procurement and Legal:

- Platform fee: Procurement is pushing for a single annual SaaS platform fee, capitalized on their books, rather than a split schedule. They requested a concrete amortized schedule to present to their CFO.
- Discount cadence: they want a simpler ladder (two breakpoints) and prefer discounts tied to committed throughput rather than node counts. Could you convert the workbook to committed tokens/month buckets?
- Security: we require the SOC2 Type II report and a contact for audit evidence; our legal team will send a redline to the term sheet.

We will return redlines by Aug 12. Also we plan to push for a two-week evaluation extension if Gate B testing requires more time.

Regards,
Ellen

> On Aug 3, 2027, at 08:47 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp plan and acceptance gates for Private VPC — commercial sequencing

Appreciate the signal and clear asks, Ellen — quick follow up with concrete next steps to keep momentum and accommodate your procurement preferences:

1) Pricing workbook update: Karthik will convert node tiers -> committed tokens/month buckets and produce an amortized platform-fee schedule (annual flat fee + monthly amortization) by Aug 11.
2) SOC2 & audit path: Marissa, can you share the SOC2 Type II stub and a named evidence contact? We’ll attach those to Gate C.
3) Legal redlines: we’ll expect your redline by Aug 12; our counsel will respond within 3 business days.
4) Evaluation window: we can extend Gate B testing by two weeks if needed; credits will be adjusted proportionally.

Proposed close timeline (updated):
- Aug 11: pricing workbook (tokens/month buckets) & platform fee amortization
- Aug 12: Acme legal redlines returned
- Aug 16: Redwood commercial response and revised term sheet
- Sep 2: Target execution of term sheet / SOW (allows finance approval cycle)

Marissa — looping you in to confirm the SOC2 stub and to draft a short onboarding runbook that maps to Gate A/B activities.

Thanks,
Jasmine

Attachment references: commercial-sequence-v1.xlsx; acme-security-checklist.docx
